thread:
sara: follow-up from today's design sync: we need a non-blocking reclaim path for host-backed pages so inference threads don't stall waiting on compaction. this came up after the 3pm stress test where a few requests hit p999 due to sync compaction.

ivan: +1. observed that synchronous reclamation during request-critical paths is the main culprit. proposed: always do reclamation in two phases 30 try in-line fast reclaim that only frees fully idle pages, otherwise enqueue async reclaim and continue. return a lightweight hint to scheduler about increased backlog.

marta: sounds reasonable. what do we do about memory pressure when async queue grows? we can't let backlog grow forever on Dedicated.

devon: add a soft cap on async queue length per-GPU (pages or bytes) and once exceeded start rejecting low-priority reclaim candidates or throttle new allocations with a backoff. also emit a metric "host_reclaim_queue_bytes".

isan: typo 3 meant ivan :)

ivan: ha. re: backpressure, how about a reclaim_credit mechanism? each tenant gets X credits per minute, async reclaim costs credits, credits refill slowly. if credits exhausted, we fall back to immediate synchronous reclaim (with potential latency hit) or reject new microbatch requests if configured. credits give predictable behavior for multi-tenant Dedicated.

marta: credits are interesting but complex. Could we start simpler: cap queue at 64MB per GPU, when exceeded mark tenant as "reclaim_throttled" and surface that in tenant diagnostics; ops can then either bump cap or trigger immediate compaction. For Private, let admins set the cap.

devon: agreed simpler is fine to iterate. also need a compaction_priority flag: background vs urgent. urgent compactions should be scheduled when p999 latency is above threshold or when queue cap is hit. background compaction runs during idle windows only.

sara: we should also pick sane defaults: inline fast reclaim window = 30ms, async enqueue threshold if page untouched > 200ms, queue cap 64MB, urgent threshold p999 > 250ms.

ci-bot: build status: ci/pipelines/offload-async-reclaim passed (job 5521).

ivan: API/Config sketch for Private YAML: 

reclaim: mode: hybrid  # hybrid | sync | async
inline_fast_ms: 30
async_touch_ms: 200
queue_cap_bytes: 67108864
urgent_p999_ms: 250

marta: please include telemetry: reclaim_path (inline|async|sync), reclaim_latency_ms, reclaim_queue_bytes, tenant_reclaim_throttled. that's how we'll know whether defaults work.

devon: one implementation note: async enqueue must preserve page metadata like last_touch and refcount. we should snapshot minimal metadata on enqueue to avoid races. also allow compactor to cancel queued items if page is reused before compaction starts.

ivan: good point. queue should hold lightweight descriptors and a fast lookup to cancel.

sara: action items: ivan/proto -> implement enqueue/cancel + queue cap in staging; devon -> compaction priority changes; marta -> draft RFC appendix with defaults and config schema. target: staging canary in 3 days.

ci-bot: staging canary scheduled: infra/canary/async-reclaim v1 (job 5599).

marta: ok thanks team. if anyone on eng-runtime has objections to defaults (30ms inline, 200ms touch, 64MB cap), speak up in next 12h or i'll lock them in the RFC. :thumbsup:
